mechanism_narrative: The four-week downward momentum in RETAIL_REC, from -13.6 to -20.0, reflects persistent avoidance and closure effects. In the absence of a visible reversal, this trend continues and pulls the next 28-day mean below the last 28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined from -13.6 to -20.0 over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: The mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility is improving from -9.9 to -4.4 while TRANSIT remains slightly positive around +2.6. Jointly these signal a gradual return of routine commuting that should lift retail-and-recreation footfall with a four-week lag, raising RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -9.9 to -4.4 and TRANSIT stayed near +2.6
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES > -5 and TRANSIT > 0, the next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC fails to exceed the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM remains strongly positive at +10.7, even though it has fallen from +17.6. Continued precautionary grocery activity above +10 diverts time and spending from discretionary retail, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises above the last 28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +10.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is negative and has worsened to -17.9. When PARKS is below -15, outdoor recreation avoidance spills over into fewer combined retail-and-recreation trips, so RETAIL_REC should decline further over the next week.
failure_condition: After a PARKS reading below -15, RETAIL_REC improves over the following week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES is less negative but RESIDENTIAL remains elevated above +4. This hybrid pattern keeps many workers near home, sustaining residential activity while commercial retail footfall stays weak, so RETAIL_REC remains below its recent mean.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES reached -4.4 while RESIDENTIAL stayed at +5.1
failure_condition: When WORKPLACES > -5 and RESIDENTIAL > 4, the next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above +3 signals relaxation of movement constraints. Once TRANSIT exceeds +3, retail-and-recreation mobility should follow upward as trips normalize, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: After TRANSIT exceeds +3 for one week, the next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week RETAIL_REC drop greater than 2 points, such as the move from -17.0 to -20.0, marks tightening restrictions. Such drops trigger further retail decline over the following two weeks as closures and caution spread.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -17.0 to -20.0 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: After a week-on-week RETAIL_REC drop greater than 2 points, the next 28-day mean RETAIL_REC exceeds the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The usual spring lift is not visible: GROCERY_PHARM is fading from +17.6 to +10.7 while PARKS remains below -17.9. This home-centered pattern starves retail-and-recreation of seasonal rebound, so RETAIL_REC stays lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell to +10.7 and PARKS fell to -17.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises above the last 28-day mean despite GROCERY_PHARM fading and PARKS staying negative.
